dedupe_keys.name: openhie facility registry specification master facility list requirements

description: This specification defines what a health facility registry should do within the OpenHIE architecture for national health information exchanges. OpenHIE is an open community of practice that publishes reference architectures used by ministries of health and their partners. The registry is described as the central authority that collects, stores and shares a current, standardised master facility list (MFL). The specification sets out workflow requirements, such as querying facility and health worker records, and functional requirements: defining and evolving the attribute data dictionary, maintaining multi-level hierarchies of facilities and administrative areas, collecting a minimum attribute set drawn from the WHO and USAID master facility list guidance (name, type, ownership, address, contacts, operational status, administrative area, coordinates, unique identifier, services offered, health workforce, opening hours and infrastructure such as power and water), user roles and permissions, and standards-based RESTful interfaces with import and export. Coverage is generic for any country. The guide is free to read online; the licence is not stated on the page. Caveats: it is a requirements document, not a dataset or software, and implementations such as DHIS2 or FHIR-based registries vary. Simulation uses: a template for assembling consistent health facility inventories as inputs to healthcare access and resilience models. Related records: healthsites.io (data-healthsites-io) and the Malawi facility registry (data-malawi-health-facilities-registry-dhis2) are examples of facility lists.
